weekly_marks.summary:
### Weekly summary for operator

Closed the week +$24.59 (+0.25%) on a $10,000 book — green, but only barely participating. Held 2 positions: SPY 2.4 sh (+1.1%) and QQQ 1.0 sh (+1.0%), with 76% cash. The week's setup was stacked-binary (FOMC 4/29 + MSFT/META/AAPL/AMZN earnings cluster), so the small initial scout (7% pre-FOMC) was correct risk management — META/MSFT got punished post-print and we sidestepped. Two good adds (SPY post-FOMC, QQQ on 4/30) lifted deployment from 7% → 24%. **The recurring failure is the same as prior weeks: ended Friday at ATH in a confirmed wk≥3 TREND-UP still under the 25% floor, with "plan to add Monday" deferrals.** Playbook now has explicit floor-enforcement language, sequencing rules (fill existing positions before scouting new ones), and a retired "wait for confirmation next week" phrasing that has been the under-deployment tell. Going into 5/4, bias is to lift to 30–35% deployed in SPY/QQQ by mid-week, trim if NFP risk builds Thu. Watchlist suggestions: add IWM/XLF/XLE for breadth, deprioritize TSLA/AMD.

### Weekly summary for operator

Closed +$116.16 (+1.16%) on a $10,024.59 starting NAV — best weekly print to date, NAV $10,140.75. Two positions did the work: SPY 2.4 sh +3.4% and QQQ 2.0 sh +6.1%. Deployment 31.5% (above wk≥3 floor of 25%); cash 68.5%. **The week's wins were process wins:** Monday QQQ add @ $672.88 lifted us above the floor on day 1, then we held discipline through NFP — no adds, no chases, no single names. NFP came in strong, market absorbed it, both ETFs closed at ATH. **The week's miss is the same one as the prior two weeks, dressed differently:** Monday plan said "optionally add SPY tranche Tue/Wed to push to 38%" — tape was constructive, VIX dropped, breadth confirmed, and we still didn't pull the trigger; then on Friday cited a 10-day-old Iran headline as the fresh reason to defer. SPY ran from $720 to $737 without us. Playbook now retires "plan to add Monday" language, adds an upper-deployment-target Wed revisit rule, and bans persistent-overhang excuses unless there's an actual same-session catalyst. Next week is a binary: **Powell's term as Fed Chair expires 5/15** — full trade tree journaled. Default stance: hold current 31.5% through 5/15, then add to ~40% on a market-friendly resolution or trim on a politicized pick. Watchlist updated to add XLF/IWM/XLE/TLT and finally retire TSLA/AMD from the active list.

### Weekly summary for operator

Closed the week **flat: −$0.88 (−0.01%)** on a $10,140.75 starting NAV; NAV $10,139.87, lifetime +1.40%. Zero trades all week, by design. This was a stacked-binary week — CPI hot (3.8%), PPI shock (6.0% YoY, multi-year high), and Powell resigned as Fed Chair Friday 5/15 with successor unnamed. SPY/QQQ printed ATH closes Thu ($748/$720) then sold off −1.2/−1.5% Fri; both positions ended green (+3.66%/+5.76%) and never tested stops. The hold-through-binary rule worked cleanly. The week's *miss* was failing to bank a partial trim Thu at ATH ahead of a known Fri binary while sitting on +5–7% gains — added a new "partial-trim into known Friday binary" heuristic. Also added a new "TREND-UP but macro regime impaired" floor row (20% min) for environments where the tape is up but rates/PPI undercut the regime — that applies now given 6% PPI and long end >5%. Retired the perennial "if binary resolves cleanly, add to 40%" branch (un-executed two weeks running) in favor of pre-defined quantitative triggers ("SPY > $745 + VIX < 17 → add 1 tranche"). Watchlist: XLF/TLT/IWM must be quoted by Tue or come off; TSLA/AMD finally removed. Going into 5/18, default stance is hold 31.5% deployed (above impaired floor of 20%), with pre-defined add/trim triggers in the playbook.

### Weekly summary for operator

Closed +$31.86 (+0.31%) on a $10,140.75 starting NAV — NAV $10,172.61, lifetime +1.73%. **Zero trades**, by design. SPY +0.94% / QQQ +1.65% on the week, both positions ended +4.57% / +7.05% open. The V-shape Mon dip (SPY $731 / QQQ $695 on 10Y 4.13% + Iran headline) was held cleanly without testing stops, then mid-week oil plunge + NVDA beat + Powell-final-FOMC drove tape to fresh Fri highs. Three process wins: (1) passed on the QQQ partial-trim into NVDA earnings after thinking through low bar / fresh macro tailwind — print was positive; (2) held the V-shape without panic-trimming; (3) finally killed XLF/TLT/IWM from the watchlist after confirming no harness data. The miss is the same one we keep re-discovering: a +0.31% NAV print on a +0.94% SPY week is exactly what 31.7% deployment buys you, and we sat at the bottom of the discretionary band (20–35%) all week despite a confirmed trend, no binary, and VIX-equivalent low. The $745 add-trigger fired Friday — we'd written "Mon only," which disqualified it. Playbook now widens the add window to Mon–Thu, adds a bottom-of-band forcing rule (must add by Wed if still at the bottom third with constructive tape), and adds an instant-availability test for new watchlist names. Going into 5/25, default stance is hold 31.7% with explicit add gates at SPY > $750 or Wed-close still-at-bottom-of-band; trim gates at SPY < $720 or 10Y > 4.65% sustained.
